messages:
maria-ops: heads up — ACME (private VPC) reporting intermittent 403s when our control plane tries to call their KMS HSM key wrap endpoint. Started ~09:20 PT. Customer says audit logs also not appearing for some requests.

devon-se: that's bad. do we have a repro? any correlation with deployments/changes?

maria-ops: customer shared a quick repro from their bastion. calls to https://kms.acme.internal:8443/keys/decrypt return 403 only when proxied through their corporate HTTP proxy. direct calls (via NAT) succeed. they suspect proxy strips auth headers. logs attached.

olivia-sre: can you paste the minimal repro here? even a curl that fails through the proxy vs direct.

maria-ops: sure — from their bastion:

```
# direct (works)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ey..." https://kms.acme.internal:8443/v1/decrypt
* Connected to kms.acme.internal (10.0.14.23) port 8443
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "plaintext": "..." }

# via corporate proxy (403)
export http_proxy=http://10.0.0.5:3128
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ey..." https://kms.acme.internal:8443/v1/decrypt
* Connected to 10.0.0.5 (10.0.0.5) port 3128
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{ "error": "missing auth" }
```

maria-ops: they also ran tcpdump and show the Authorization header not present once it leaves the proxy.

devon-se: so the proxy is mutating/removing the header. is the proxy doing TLS MITM or CONNECT? if it's plain HTTP proxy to an HTTPS origin, the client should use CONNECT and proxy shouldn't touch headers.

maria-ops: customer says their proxy does an SSL intercept for inspection (corporate policy). they admitted squid-like filtering that strips some headers unless explicitly allowed.

ryan-security: that would explain both the 403 and missing audit logs — our control plane's requests are authenticated via the Authorization header. if header is dropped, KMS rejects and audit subsystem never records a successful key op (so missing entries). also possible billing attribution depends on request metadata that gets lost.

olivia-sre: can we confirm the control plane attempted the requests? sre-bot: ingest shows attempts from infra-eu-2 at 09:21:12 -> target kms.acme.internal:8443, status 403.

sre-bot: event: controlplane.request id=cp_9a12 host=kms.acme.internal:8443 status=403 src=10.45.8.23 time=2026-03-12T16:21:12Z

maria-ops: customer also sees missing entries in their audit collector for ~09:20-09:27. they widened logging and captured the proxy config snippet:

```
# corporate-proxy.conf (excerpt)
# default header blacklist
header_access Authorization deny all
header_access Proxy-Authorization deny all
```

devon-se: ugh. so their default squid config denies Authorization. two problems: (1) customer side policy — they need to allow Authorization for our controlplane IPs, and (2) on our side we should fall back to a more robust auth mechanism when operating in proxied environments (e.g., short-lived certs + mTLS).

ryan-security: action items: (A) request temporary allowlist from customer for control plane IPs to bypass inspection for kms.acme.internal:8443, (B) provide them a recommended proxy config line to preserve header for that host, and (C) open internal incident to design mTLS fallback for private deployments.

maria-ops: suggested proxy config to customer:

```
# allow Authorization header for this host
acl _allow_kms dstdomain .kms.acme.internal
header_access Authorization allow _allow_kms
```

maria-ops: customer asked for a short repro patch we can run from our side to validate if they update proxy rules. I can run a quick curl from control plane via their proxy if they permit.

olivia-sre: before we touch their prod, we should ask for a temporary window and run from a staging controlplane node. we need IAM approval from security. @ryan-security can you sign off for a one-hour window?

ryan-security: yes, +1 for a scheduled 1-hour remediation window. require: (1) customer PR to proxy config, (2) time window, (3) we will only run a single health-check curl against kms endpoint, no key material in logs.

devon-se: for tracking: creating a bug and CCing infra and platform. propose short-term mitigation: document proxy requirements in Private/VPC onboarding (FAQ) and add test that verifies Authorization header preserved during onboarding network checks. long-term: mTLS to avoid header fragility.

maria-ops: customer also reported billing delta — tokens/usage for some transactions showed zero on their account for that window. likely because controlplane rejected requests before attribution header attached. I'll include that in the ticket.

olivia-sre: can someone paste the minimal steps we'll ask the customer to run after they change proxy? that'll speed the verification window.

maria-ops: yes — ask them to update squid, then from bastion run:

```
export http_proxy=http://10.0.0.5:3128
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-token>" https://kms.acme.internal:8443/v1/decrypt
# expect HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

maria-ops: if that passes, we'll re-run control plane smoke check and confirm audit logs show entries and billing attribution reconciles.

ryan-security: also document: do NOT allow broad bypass. prefer host-specific rule for kms.acme.internal and limited time window. add expiry to their proxy ACL change.

devon-se: assigned: DEVON -> investigate mTLS fallback and onboarding test, OLIVIA -> schedule staging check and run smoke curl after customer confirms, MARIA -> coordinate with customer and collect updated proxy config + tcpdump, RYAN -> approve window and review customer security posture for temporary exception.

maria-ops: noted. customer is prepping the proxy ACL change now. I'll update here when they confirm. thanks all :heart:

customer-logs-bot: acme: proxy ACL change scheduled 2026-03-12T17:00:00Z by acme-netops, ticket #ACME-447.

maria-ops: sweet — we'll aim for a 17:00 UTC check. will ping teams 10min prior.
